'''Rajendran Raja''' (14 July 1948 – 15 February 2014) was an Indian-American physicist who played a key role in the discovery of the [[top quark]] at [[Fermilab]].

==Early life and education==

Rajendran Raja was born on 14 July 1948 in [[Guruvayur]], India. His mother was a chemist and his father was a geophysicist. After his mother died when he was nine years old, his father remarried and moved the family to Kenya, where Raja's father taught at the [[University of Nairobi]]. Raja attended a Kenyan boarding school and [[Strathmore University]] in [[Nairobi]], Kenya. He traveled to England in 1967 to attend the [[University of Cambridge]],<ref name="Chicago Tribune">{{cite news |last=Kates |first=Joan Giangrasse |date=27 February 2014 |title=Rajendran Raja 1948-2014: Former Fermilab physicist helped discover top quark, Higgs boson |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2014/02/27/rajendran-raja-1948-2014/ |newspaper=Chicago Tribune |location=Chicago, Illinois |publisher=Tribune Company |access-date=4 June 2014 }}</ref> where he received his undergraduate degree in 1970. He remained at this institution to pursue his PhD under the direction of John Gordon Rushbrooke<ref name="Inspire">{{cite web |url=https://inspirehep.net/record/992393 |title=Rajendran Raja |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |website=Inspire HEP |accessdate=4 June 2014}}</ref> and was inducted as a fellow of the [[University of Cambridge]]'s Trinity College in 1973.<ref name="Chicago Tribune"/> He received his PhD in 1975<ref name="Inspire"/> with a thesis titled ''Single Pion Production''.<ref name="Cambridge">{{cite web |url=http://alumni.trin.cam.ac.uk/file/RajendranRaja_obituary.pdf |title=Rajendran Raja (1948-2014) |author=Sateesh Mane |website=Trinity Members Online |accessdate=5 June 2014}}</ref>

==Career==

In 1974, Rajendran Raja immigrated to the United States and became a physicist at [[Fermilab]], a [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]] [[United States Department of Energy national laboratories|national laboratory]] near [[Batavia, Illinois]] specializing in high-energy [[particle physics]]. During his forty years at Fermilab, Raja's important contributions to the lab's scientific work included playing a key role in the design of the hermetic [[D0 experiment|DZero]] detector. He served as head of the [[top quark]] analysis group, and the multivariate algorithm he developed was a crucial tool in the discovery of this particle at [[Fermilab]] in 1995. During his last years at [[Fermilab]], he served as spokesperson for the Main Injector Particle Production experiment. He also became an advocate of accelerator-driven [[Thorium fuel cycle|thorium reactors]], which he believed could help solve the world's energy crisis. He contributed more than 300 publications to scientific journals.{{citation needed|date=October 2018}}

Raja also fostered cooperation between the U.S. and India in particle physics, starting a program at [[D0 experiment|DZero]] in the early 1990s that has helped more than ten Indian students earn their PhDs.<ref name="Fermilab Today">{{cite news |last1=Mishra |first1=Shekhar |last2=Beharelle |first2=Aaron |date=18 February 2014 |title=In memoriam: Rajendran Raja |url=http://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/archive/archive_2014/today14-02-18.html |newspaper=Fermilab Today |location=Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois |publisher=Fermi Research Alliance |accessdate=5 June 2014 }}</ref>
